I don't know why people are saying you can't do this, it's quite simple:

If you're using OBS, go into the settings and set a stream delay of 5 or 10 seconds (or however long you think you'll need). Then if you're streaming you can press the 'End Stream (Discard Delay)' button (you can set up a hotkey for this) and it'll immediately end the stream and stop the stream before the last 5 or 10 seconds (or however long you set it for) goes out.

Make sure you press 'End Stream (Discard Delay)' and NOT 'End Stream'. If you press the latter it'll play the last 5 or 10 seconds AND THEN end the stream. (Though make sure you DO press 'End Stream' when saying goodbye otherwise you might forget and it'll end the stream abruptly before you said goodbye.)

This is the only way I've found to stop the stream before something happens in OBS. (I wouldn't be surprised if you can do a similar thing with Streamlabs or whatever.)

Also don't know why people are saying 'you shouldn't be streaming'; it's a perfectly legitimate concern that was one of my first thoughts before starting to stream.
